jobs.title: Director, Operational Technology (OT)
jobs.description:
Job Description

As a global technology leader, Honeywell Process Technology (PT) enables the energy evolution, provides solutions that reduce emissions, and delivers innovative sustainable materials to our customers across industries. We are committed to driving sustainable practices and enhancing energy efficiency through cutting-edge technology and innovative solutions. Our team is dedicated to creating a sustainable future by empowering industries to transition toward cleaner energy sources and reduce their carbon footprint. Join us in our mission to make the world a more sustainable place while delivering exceptional value to our customers.

As Director of IT for OT, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering technology capabilities that enable resilient, efficient, and scalable supply chain and plant operations across PT. This role will lead OT optimization and maintenance, with a strong emphasis on governance, cybersecurity, execution and compliance, while building and managing a high‑performing, multi‑disciplinary team to ensure technology investments deliver measurable business value and align with PT priorities.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities:

Define and execute PT OT strategy to optimize manufacturing systems—including MES, SCADA, PLCs, and data historians—to improve plant reliability, scalability, and operational performance.
Ensure standardization, lifecycle management, and cyber-secure deployment of OT systems across manufacturing sites, ensuring consistency, resilience, and risk mitigation.
Align OT architecture and data flows with ENIT systems to enable smart factory capabilities, digital manufacturing, and integrated operational insight.
Partner with site leadership and operations to prioritize OT investments, balance innovation with operational stability, and minimize disruption to plant execution.
Ensure robust governance, support models, and compliance frameworks are in place across OT environments, with a strong emphasis on cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, and safe operations.

Leadership & Financial Management

Lead and develop a high‑performing, multi‑disciplinary global team across OT, setting clear expectations and driving accountability for results.
Lead the M&A Infrastructure, Operations and Security Team
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement, enabling teams to deliver results in a fast‑paced, matrixed environment.
Own and manage OT technology budgets, ensuring investments are aligned with PT business priorities and deliver measurable value and return on investment.
Establish and monitor KPIs and value realization metrics, making data‑driven course corrections to ensure operational, financial, and strategic objectives are met or exceeded.

Qualifications

Must Haves

A minimum of 8 years of experience in IT infrastructure management and/or ISC platforms.
Proven experience managing OT initiatives.

WE VALUE 

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
Master's degree in IT or related field
Leadership experience in two or more Information Technology, Engineering or Strategy functional areas 
Proven experience leading ERP transformations
Strong understanding of network architecture and security principles.
Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Proven ability to drive strategic initiatives and foster collaboration across cross-functional teams.
Familiarity with compliance standards and regulations related to IT infrastructure.
Strong technical, quantitative, and analytical skills 
Experience in the manufacturing or chemical industry
Knowledge of cybersecurity and data privacy best practices Project management certification (e.g., PMP)
Understanding of key information technology solutions and practices 
Strong business/financial acumen and ability to translate new technology into business value 

The annual base salary range for this position in Illinois is $177,000 - $221,000. This position is incentive plan eligible. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.

In addition to a competitive salary, leading-edge work, and developing solutions side-by-side with dedicated experts in their fields, Honeywell employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. This package includes employer subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, EAP, and Educational Assistance; Parental Leave, Paid Time Off (for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave), and 12 Paid Holidays. For more information visit: Benefits at Honeywell

The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

About Us

Honeywell Technologies is a global, pure-play automation company with a legacy of innovating to help solve the world’s most mission-critical challenges, enhancing the quality of life for people and communities around the world. We serve the building, industrial and process sectors with a broad portfolio of services, solutions and products, underpinned by our Honeywell Technologies Accelerator operating system and Honeywell Technologies Forge intelligence layer. By combining the deep domain expertise of our more than 50,000 employees with decades of data from our global installed base, we are uniquely positioned to lead the industrial sector’s transition from automation to autonomy.

jobs.title: Senior Director of Corporate IT
jobs.description:
Company Description
NAM A BANK is a growing financial institution focused on delivering reliable, innovative banking services to a diverse customer base. The organization emphasizes secure, technology-driven solutions to support retail and corporate clients. NAM A BANK values integrity, operational excellence, and strong risk management practices across all business units. Team members are encouraged to contribute to continuous improvement, digital transformation, and customer-centric innovation. The bank offers opportunities for professional development and leadership in a dynamic, technology-focused environment.
Role Description
The Senior Director of Corporate IT is a full-time remote role responsible for leading the overall IT function across NAM A BANK’s corporate operations. This position oversees IT strategy, governance, and architecture to align technology initiatives with business objectives, regulatory requirements, and risk management standards. Day-to-day responsibilities include directing IT operations, supervising infrastructure and application support, and ensuring the stability, scalability, and security of core banking systems and networks. The role also manages IT budgets, vendor relationships, and technology procurement, while driving digital transformation projects and process optimization efforts. The Senior Director collaborates closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to prioritize initiatives, lead incident response and business continuity planning, and foster a culture of innovation, compliance, and cybersecurity awareness.
Qualifications

Candidates should possess strong IT Management and IT Operations skills to lead enterprise-wide technology teams and services.
Candidates should possess solid Information Technology and IT Strategy skills to design and execute long-term technology roadmaps aligned with business goals.
Candidates should possess hands-on Network Security experience to protect systems, data, and communications in a regulated financial environment.
Candidates should possess experience with governance, risk, and compliance frameworks, particularly in banking or financial services.
Candidates should possess leadership and people management abilities, including coaching, performance management, and cross-functional collaboration.
Candidates should possess strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to manage complex projects and competing priorities.
Candidates should possess excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to present technical topics to non-technical stakeholders.
Relevant academic background such as a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; professional certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, ITIL, PMP) are beneficial.

jobs.title: Technology Strategy Senior Manager
jobs.description:
We are Lenovo. We do what we say. We own what we do. We WOW our customers.

Lenovo is a US$83 billion revenue global technology powerhouse, ranked #153 in the Fortune Global 500, and serving millions of customers every day in 180 markets. Focused on a bold vision to deliver Smarter Technology for All, Lenovo has built on its success as the world’s largest PC company with a full-stack portfolio of AI-enabled, AI-ready, and AI-optimized devices (PCs, workstations, smartphones, tablets), infrastructure (server, storage, edge, high performance computing and software defined infrastructure), software, solutions, and services. Lenovo’s continued investment in world-changing innovation is building a more equitable, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. Lenovo is listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange under Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY).

This transformation together with Lenovo’s world-changing innovation is building a more inclusive, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. To find out more visit www.lenovo.com, and read about the latest news via our StoryHub.

The Enterprise AI Technology Strategy team enables Lenovo to make better technology investment decisions by identifying emerging opportunities, generating strategic options, evaluating trade-offs, aligning stakeholders, and translating technology insight into business impact. As part of the CTO Organization, this team helps determine where Lenovo should play, how it can win, and where it should invest, partner, or accelerate across AI and emerging technologies.

This position is working in the heart of the most significant technology strategy planning and development group in the CTO Organization. We are recruiting people with passion about technologies that thrive in an environment where curiosity and entrepreneurship is encouraged.

Roles And Responsibilities

Lead enterprise-level assessments of emerging AI technologies, ecosystem developments, industry shifts, and competitive dynamics to identify strategic opportunities and risks.
Develop technology outlooks, strategic perspectives, investment theses, future scenarios, and recommendations that shape Lenovo’s long-term AI and technology strategy.
Lead the evaluation of AI platforms, agentic AI frameworks, enterprise AI architectures, and emerging technology ecosystems to determine strategic implications and investment priorities.
Apply strategic frameworks to evaluate alternatives, assess trade-offs, and recommend where Lenovo should invest, partner, accelerate, differentiate, or intentionally not compete.
Shape innovation priorities and strategic direction across RD organizations.
Drive enterprise alignment across CTO Organization, Business Units, Research leadership, and executive stakeholders around shared technology priorities and strategic outcomes.
Translate complex technology trends into clear decision frameworks and executive recommendations.
Lead cross-functional strategic initiatives that align technology investments with long-term business objectives.
Facilitate executive discussions, strategic planning activities, decision forums, and stakeholder alignment efforts.
Support strategic execution by connecting technology strategy to planning, governance, investment, and operational processes.
Serve as a trusted advisor to CTO leadership and other senior leaders on AI and emerging technology strategy.
Mentor team members and help elevate strategic thinking and analytical rigor across the organization.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Technology Management, or a related field.
10+ years of experience in technology strategy, corporate strategy, innovation, management consulting, enterprise architecture, product strategy, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-scale technology strategy initiatives and influencing senior leadership decisions.
Experience developing strategic recommendations, investment theses, business cases, and executive-level communications.
Experience engaging with cross-functional stakeholders across technology, research, product, engineering, and business organizations.
Proven record of translating emerging technology trends into strategic business decisions and organizational action.
Understanding of enterprise AI concepts including foundation models, agentic AI, RAG, model evaluation, orchestration, AI governance, and enterprise AI platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in a related discipline, including MBA.
Experience working within large global technology organizations.
Hands-on experience building, deploying, or evaluating enterprise AI and agentic AI solutions.
Experience leading strategic planning, portfolio management, investment governance, or corporate development initiatives.
Experience facilitating executive workshops, planning sessions, and decision-making forums.
Background in top-tier strategy consulting, corporate strategy, or senior product strategy roles.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Technology Risk Management (Cyber Threat & Insider Risk)
jobs.description:
Your opportunity

At Schwab, you’re empowered to make an impact on your career. Here, innovative thought meets creative problem solving, helping us challenge the status quo and transform the finance industry together. We believe in the importance of in-office collaboration and fully intend for the selected candidate for this role to work on site in the specified location(s).

As Schwab continues to expand its technology footprint across cloud, artificial intelligence, digital platforms, applications & APIs, and infrastructure services, the Technology Risk Management (TRM) team plays a critical role in helping ensure the company maintains a strong risk posture through independent oversight and risk-informed assurance activities.

TRM has an opening in the Cyber Threat & Insider Risk discipline for an individual contributor to serve as the primary subject matter expert for second line oversight, effective challenge, and risk reporting of Security Operations, Digital Forensics, and Incident Response capabilities, processes, and controls. More specifically, this role reviews risks and control activities over cyber detection, monitoring, investigation, containment, and response. You will assess control effectiveness, identify systemic weaknesses, and ensure alignment with enterprise policies and standards, regulatory expectations, and industry best practices. You will review and challenge issue identification, closure, risk acceptances related to risks in your domain. You will maintain visibility into the firm's emerging threats and implementation of AI technologies and influence the implementation of expected monitoring, investigation, and response control activities. Success requires a self-starter attitude, strong desire to learn, building collaborative relationships with business partners, and the ability to assess and communicate technical risk clearly to executive, committee, regulatory, and technical audiences.

Please note: This position is Monday through Friday during standard business hours and follows a hybrid work model with four days in the office and one day working from home. The role is available only in Indianapolis, IN; Omaha, NE; Austin, TX and Southlake, TX (DFW). Candidates must reside in or be willing to relocate at their own expense to one of the listed locations.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without employer sponsorship.

What you have

To ensure that we have fulfilled our promise of "challenging the status quo," this role has specific qualifications that successful candidates should have.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of experience in Risk Management, Cybersecurity, or Internal Audit
Demonstrated Risk Assessment, Risk Identification, and Risk Prioritization experience
Ability to apply Analytical Thinking and Problem Solving to complex technology risk information
Strong Communication skills with the ability to present clear conclusions to technical and executive audiences
Demonstrated Collaboration and Stakeholder Management Influence skills across multiple functions and organizational levels

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree
CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, or an equivalent technology risk, cybersecurity, audit certification
Experience identifying and assessing risks associated with security operations, digital forensics, and/or cybersecurity incident response
Financial services industry experience
Demonstrated Self-Starter, Influencing Others, and Building Collaborative Relationship competencies in an evolving environment

In addition to the salary range, this role is also eligible for bonus or incentive opportunities

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan
Paid time for vacation, volunteering, and 28-day sabbatical after every 5 years of service for eligible positions
Paid parental leave and family building benefits
Tuition reimbursement
Health, dental, and vision insurance

jobs.title: Director, Technology
jobs.description:
Find YOUR fit at Ohio CAT Rental Store (a division of Ohio Machinery Co.)!  Join a winning culture that strives to be the top-performing, dynamic industry leader and partner of choice for the products and solutions that help our customers build, improve, feed, power, and protect our world.  Come grow your career - See what opportunities await today!  
Work Arrangements: Onsite: This position is fully onsite.
Summary: 
The Director, Technology is responsible for developing and executing the dealership’s technology strategy to drive customer productivity, safety, equipment utilization and profitability. This role serves as the technology business owner for the dealership leading the adoption and growth of Caterpillar technology solutions including Visionlink, Cat Grade, Detect, Payload, productivity, Command, Connectivity, Telematics, and emerging digital technologies
The Director will work cross functionally across Sales, Rental, Product Support, Marketing, Digital, Operations, and IT to ensure the successful deployment, training, support and growth of technology solutions throughout the dealer territory. The position will also maintain strategic relationships with Caterpillar, Trimble, and any other technology partners.
Essential Functions and Responsibilities:
Strategic Leadership: Develop and execute the dealer’s technology growth strategy and annual business plan.
Establish technology-related revenue, adoption, and customer success objections.
Lead technology initiatives that improve customer productivity, safety, machine utilization, and operational efficiency.
Serve as the dealership’s primary advocate for technology-driven business transformation.
Present technology performance, KPI’s and strategic recommendations to executive and senior leadership.

Sales & Business Development:
Drive sales growth of Caterpillar technology products and services.
Support machine and aftermarket sales teams with technology expertise and solution selling.
Develop go-to-market strategies or technology-enabled offerings.
Collaborate with Major Accounts, Rental Product Support and Sales leadership to increase technology penetration.
Maintain relationships with Caterpillar technology organizations, Trimble, and other strategic partners.
Develop and implement predelivery expectations at all branches for incoming Cat Products where technology offerings apply. 

Customer Adoption & Success:
Establish customer onboarding and utilization programs for technology products. 
Monitor customer adoption rates and develop plans to increase engagement.
Ensure customers are realizing value from technology investments through measurable outcomes. 
Lead customer demonstrations, training events, and executive-level technology discussions.

Products Support & Operations:
Develop processes for technology installation, activation, commissioning, and support. 
Coordinate resources supporting integrated machine technologies and telematics solutions
Work with service operations to ensure technology support capabilities remain aligned with customer needs.
Create and maintain standard operating procedures for technology deployment and support. 

Team Leadership:
Recruit, lead, coach, and develop technology specialists, trainers, and support personnel.
Establish accountability for performance, customer satisfaction, technology adoption, and financial objectives 
Build a culture focused on customer success innovation, continuous improvement, and collaboration.
Partner with Sales, Rental and Product Support leadership to establish technology champions throughout the organization.

Performance Management:
Develop and track key performance indicators including: Technology revenue growth, VisionLink adoption, Cat Grade order rates, Subscription renewals, Customer utilization rates, Technology attachment rates, and Customer satisfaction metrics. 
Monitor profitability and ROI of technology initiatives.
Provide regular reporting to dealership leadership and Caterpillar.

Minimum Skills and Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in business, Engineering, Construction Management, Information Technology, or related field required. MBA or advanced degree preferred.
Minimum 10 years of experience in heavy equipment, construction technology, digital solutions, product support, equipment sales, or related industries.
Minimum 5 years of leadership or management experience.
Ability and willingness to travel up to 50-60% of the time, including overnight travel as needed.
Experience with Caterpillar, SITECH, Trimble, Top Con, telematics, fleet management, or construction technology preferred. 
Proven success developing and executing strategic business plans.
Demonstrated ability to lead organizational change initiatives.
Strong understanding of:
Caterpillar technology products
Telematics and connectivity solutions
Fleet management systems
Construction and mining applicants 
Product support operations

Equipment sales and rental operations
Strong financial and business acumen.
Excellent communication and presentation skills.
Ability to influence across departments and all levels of the organization.
Strong project management and change management capabilities.

Employee Benefits:
401(k): Match and employer discretionary contribution.
Health Insurance: Two options are available, including an HSA with a dollar-for-dollar match of up to $1,200 per year.
Dental & Vision Insurance: Comprehensive coverage options.
Financial Access: Credit Union membership is available.
Insurance: Life Insurance, Short-Term Disability, and Long-Term Disability coverage.
Educational Opportunities: Scholarships for employees’ spouses and children through the Ohio Machinery Education and Opportunity Foundation.
Compensation: Base pay, annual bonus potential, and company success share bonuses.

Physical Requirements:
Primary functions require sufficient physical ability and mobility to work in an office setting; to stand or sit for prolonged periods; to occasionally stoop, bend, kneel, crouch, reach, and twist; to lift, carry, push, and/or pull light to moderate amounts of weight; to operate office equipment requiring repetitive hand movement and fine coordination including use of a computer keyboard; and to verbally communicate to exchange information. The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet in office settings and moderate to loud in other situations, with both constant and sudden loud noises possible.

jobs.title: Senior Information Technology Project Manager
jobs.description:
Enterprise Project Manager – IT / Public Health
Location:
Columbia, South Carolina
Work Arrangement:
Hybrid
Contract Duration:
12 months, with possible extension
Eligibility:
Must currently reside in South Carolina. Relocation is not permitted.
About the Opportunity
Computer Consultants International, Inc. (CCI) is seeking an experienced Enterprise Project Manager Consultant to support the South Carolina Department of Public Health (SC DPH).
This role will support agency-wide project management and governance initiatives, including implementation of a new Project Management System, portfolio oversight, Power BI dashboard reporting, stakeholder engagement, user training, and organizational change management.
The ideal candidate brings extensive experience managing complex IT and business projects, supporting state or federal government initiatives, implementing project management systems, and developing dashboards that improve project visibility and decision-making.
Key Responsibilities
Lead and coordinate enterprise-level IT and business projects from planning through implementation.
Support implementation and adoption of the agency's new Project Management System as the existing PWA platform is decommissioned.
Establish and maintain project management standards, governance processes, methodologies, and best practices.
Oversee project portfolios, resource coordination, project status tracking, risks, issues, and dependencies.
Create and maintain Power BI dashboards to communicate project performance, portfolio status, milestones, and management metrics.
Develop and execute change management strategies to support system implementation and organizational adoption.
Engage stakeholders across departments to gather requirements, communicate progress, and resolve project-related challenges.
Coordinate user training, documentation, and ongoing support for project management tools and processes.
Prepare project reports, executive updates, and presentations to support leadership decisions.
Support strategic initiatives aligned with the South Carolina Department of Public Health's organizational objectives.

Mandatory Qualifications
15+ years of project management experience.
10+ years of experience supporting state or federal IT projects.
10+ years of experience implementing project management systems.
8+ years of experience creating Power BI dashboards.
10+ years of change management experience.
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology or Business Administration.

Preferred Qualifications
PMP or Certified ScrumMaster (CSM) certification.
Experience implementing public health software or public health IT systems.
CompTIA A+ certification.

Work Arrangement and Interview Process
Hybrid work arrangement in South Carolina, with onsite attendance based on project needs.
Onsite visits may be required approximately once per month to once per quarter, sometimes with limited notice.
Candidates must currently reside in South Carolina; relocation is not permitted.
Two rounds of virtual interviews.
Initial 12-month contract with a possibility of extension.

Interested candidates should apply with an updated resume highlighting their enterprise project management, government IT project, project management system implementation, Power BI, and change management experience.

jobs.title: Vice President of IT Management
jobs.description:
Company Description
Merchant Serv is a comprehensive merchant services provider that supports businesses with payment processing, point-of-sale (POS) systems, and virtual assistance solutions. The organization focuses on reducing or eliminating processing fees so businesses can reinvest savings into growth and operations. It offers secure, affordable, and powerful POS hardware tailored to small business needs, along with tools for online transactions, invoicing, recurring billing, and acceptance of major credit cards. Merchant Serv emphasizes personalized service, with local account executives collaborating closely with business leaders nationwide to design custom plans aligned with specific objectives. Prospective team members join a company committed to innovative, client-centric solutions in the payments and business services space.
Role Description
The Vice President of IT Management is a full-time remote role responsible for leading Merchant Serv’s overall information technology vision, strategy, and operations. This role oversees IT governance, infrastructure, security, and application environments that support payment processing platforms, POS solutions, and internal business systems. Day-to-day responsibilities include driving IT strategy and roadmaps, prioritizing and managing technology initiatives, and ensuring high system availability, scalability, and data protection. The Vice President of IT Management collaborates with executive leadership, product, operations, and client-facing teams to align technology investments with business goals and regulatory requirements. This role also leads and mentors IT teams, manages vendor relationships, monitors budgets and performance metrics, and continuously improves processes to support a secure, efficient, and innovative technology environment.
Qualifications

Strong foundation in information technology, including enterprise systems, infrastructure, cybersecurity, and cloud-based solutions.
Demonstrated experience in IT management and leadership, including building and guiding high-performing technical teams.
Proven ability to develop and execute IT strategy aligned with business goals, particularly in payments, financial services, or technology-driven organizations.
Expertise in project management and strategic planning to oversee complex, cross-functional IT initiatives and deliver them on time and within budget.
Excellent communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences.
Experience working in or supporting remote, distributed teams and using modern collaboration tools.
Knowledge of regulatory, compliance, and security standards relevant to payment processing and financial data (e.g., PCI-DSS) is highly beneficial.
Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field; advanced degree or relevant certifications (e.g., PMP, ITIL, CISSP) are a plus.

new_jobs.description:
We are Lenovo. We do what we say. We own what we do. We WOW our customers.

Lenovo is a US$83 billion revenue global technology powerhouse, ranked #153 in the Fortune Global 500, and serving millions of customers every day in 180 markets. Focused on a bold vision to deliver Smarter Technology for All, Lenovo has built on its success as the world’s largest PC company with a full-stack portfolio of AI-enabled, AI-ready, and AI-optimized devices (PCs, workstations, smartphones, tablets), infrastructure (server, storage, edge, high performance computing and software defined infrastructure), software, solutions, and services. This transformation together with Lenovo’s world-changing innovation is building a more inclusive, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. To find out more visit www.lenovo.com, and read about the latest news via our StoryHub.

The Enterprise AI Technology Strategy team enables Lenovo to make better technology investment decisions by identifying emerging opportunities, generating strategic options, evaluating trade-offs, aligning stakeholders, and translating technology insight into business impact. As part of the CTO Organization, this team helps determine where Lenovo should play, how it can win, and where it should invest, partner, or accelerate across AI and emerging technologies.

This position is working in the heart of the most significant technology strategy planning and development group in the CTO Organization. We are recruiting people with passion about technologies that thrive in an environment where curiosity and entrepreneurship is encouraged.

Roles And Responsibilities

Lead enterprise-level assessments of emerging AI technologies, ecosystem developments, industry shifts, and competitive dynamics to identify strategic opportunities and risks.
Develop technology outlooks, strategic perspectives, investment theses, future scenarios, and recommendations that shape Lenovo’s long-term AI and technology strategy.
Lead the evaluation of AI platforms, agentic AI frameworks, enterprise AI architectures, and emerging technology ecosystems to determine strategic implications and investment priorities.
Apply strategic frameworks to evaluate alternatives, assess trade-offs, and recommend where Lenovo should invest, partner, accelerate, differentiate, or intentionally not compete.
Shape innovation priorities and strategic direction across RD organizations.
Drive enterprise alignment across CTO Organization, Business Units, Research leadership, and executive stakeholders around shared technology priorities and strategic outcomes.
Translate complex technology trends into clear decision frameworks and executive recommendations.
Lead cross-functional strategic initiatives that align technology investments with long-term business objectives.
Facilitate executive discussions, strategic planning activities, decision forums, and stakeholder alignment efforts.
Support strategic execution by connecting technology strategy to planning, governance, investment, and operational processes.
Serve as a trusted advisor to CTO leadership and other senior leaders on AI and emerging technology strategy.
Mentor team members and help elevate strategic thinking and analytical rigor across the organization.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Technology Management, or a related field.
10+ years of experience in technology strategy, corporate strategy, innovation, management consulting, enterprise architecture, product strategy, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-scale technology strategy initiatives and influencing senior leadership decisions.
Experience developing strategic recommendations, investment theses, business cases, and executive-level communications.
Experience engaging with cross-functional stakeholders across technology, research, product, engineering, and business organizations.
Proven record of translating emerging technology trends into strategic business decisions and organizational action.
Understanding of enterprise AI concepts including foundation models, agentic AI, RAG, model evaluation, orchestration, AI governance, and enterprise AI platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in a related discipline, including MBA.
Experience working within large global technology organizations.
Hands-on experience building, deploying, or evaluating enterprise AI and agentic AI solutions.
Experience leading strategic planning, portfolio management, investment governance, or corporate development initiatives.
Experience facilitating executive workshops, planning sessions, and decision-making forums.
Background in top-tier strategy consulting, corporate strategy, or senior product strategy roles.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Technology Risk Management (Cyber Threat & Insider Risk)
new_jobs.description:
Your opportunity

At Schwab, you’re empowered to make an impact on your career. Here, innovative thought meets creative problem solving, helping us challenge the status quo and transform the finance industry together. We believe in the importance of in-office collaboration and fully intend for the selected candidate for this role to work on site in the specified location(s).

As Schwab continues to expand its technology footprint across cloud, artificial intelligence, digital platforms, applications & APIs, and infrastructure services, the Technology Risk Management (TRM) team plays a critical role in helping ensure the company maintains a strong risk posture through independent oversight and risk-informed assurance activities.

TRM has an opening in the Cyber Threat & Insider Risk discipline for an individual contributor to serve as the primary subject matter expert for second line oversight, effective challenge, and risk reporting of Security Operations, Digital Forensics, and Incident Response capabilities, processes, and controls. More specifically, this role reviews risks and control activities over cyber detection, monitoring, investigation, containment, and response. You will assess control effectiveness, identify systemic weaknesses, and ensure alignment with enterprise policies and standards, regulatory expectations, and industry best practices. You will review and challenge issue identification, closure, risk acceptances related to risks in your domain. You will maintain visibility into the firm's emerging threats and implementation of AI technologies and influence the implementation of expected monitoring, investigation, and response control activities. Success requires a self-starter attitude, strong desire to learn, building collaborative relationships with business partners, and the ability to assess and communicate technical risk clearly to executive, committee, regulatory, and technical audiences.

Please note: This position is Monday through Friday during standard business hours and follows a hybrid work model with four days in the office and one day working from home. The role is available only in Indianapolis, IN; Omaha, NE; Austin, TX and Southlake, TX (DFW). Candidates must reside in or be willing to relocate at their own expense to one of the listed locations.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without employer sponsorship.

What you have

To ensure that we have fulfilled our promise of "challenging the status quo," this role has specific qualifications that successful candidates should have.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of experience in Risk Management, Cybersecurity, or Internal Audit
Demonstrated Risk Assessment, Risk Identification, and Risk Prioritization experience
Ability to apply Analytical Thinking and Problem Solving to complex technology risk information
Strong Communication skills with the ability to present clear conclusions to technical and executive audiences
Demonstrated Collaboration and Stakeholder Management Influence skills across multiple functions and organizational levels

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree
CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, or an equivalent technology risk, cybersecurity, audit certification
Experience identifying and assessing risks associated with security operations, digital forensics, and/or cybersecurity incident response
Financial services industry experience
Demonstrated Self-Starter, Influencing Others, and Building Collaborative Relationship competencies in an evolving environment

In addition to the salary range, this role is also eligible for bonus or incentive opportunities

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan
Paid time for vacation, volunteering, and 28-day sabbatical after every 5 years of service for eligible positions
Paid parental leave and family building benefits
Tuition reimbursement
Health, dental, and vision insurance

Summary: 
The Director, Technology is responsible for developing and executing the dealership’s technology strategy to drive customer productivity, safety, equipment utilization and profitability. This role serves as the technology business owner for the dealership leading the adoption and growth of Caterpillar technology solutions including Visionlink, Cat Grade, Detect, Payload, productivity, Command, Connectivity, Telematics, and emerging digital technologies
The Director will work cross functionally across Sales, Rental, Product Support, Marketing, Digital, Operations, and IT to ensure the successful deployment, training, support and growth of technology solutions throughout the dealer territory. The position will also maintain strategic relationships with Caterpillar, Trimble, and any other technology partners.
Essential Functions and Responsibilities:
Strategic Leadership: Develop and execute the dealer’s technology growth strategy and annual business plan.
Establish technology-related revenue, adoption, and customer success objections.
Lead technology initiatives that improve customer productivity, safety, machine utilization, and operational efficiency.
Serve as the dealership’s primary advocate for technology-driven business transformation.
Present technology performance, KPI’s and strategic recommendations to executive and senior leadership.

Sales & Business Development:
Drive sales growth of Caterpillar technology products and services.
Support machine and aftermarket sales teams with technology expertise and solution selling.
Develop go-to-market strategies or technology-enabled offerings.
Collaborate with Major Accounts, Rental Product Support and Sales leadership to increase technology penetration.
Maintain relationships with Caterpillar technology organizations, Trimble, and other strategic partners.
Develop and implement predelivery expectations at all branches for incoming Cat Products where technology offerings apply. 

Customer Adoption & Success:
Establish customer onboarding and utilization programs for technology products. 
Monitor customer adoption rates and develop plans to increase engagement.
Ensure customers are realizing value from technology investments through measurable outcomes. 
Lead customer demonstrations, training events, and executive-level technology discussions.

Products Support & Operations:
Develop processes for technology installation, activation, commissioning, and support. 
Coordinate resources supporting integrated machine technologies and telematics solutions
Work with service operations to ensure technology support capabilities remain aligned with customer needs.
Create and maintain standard operating procedures for technology deployment and support. 

Team Leadership:
Recruit, lead, coach, and develop technology specialists, trainers, and support personnel.
Establish accountability for performance, customer satisfaction, technology adoption, and financial objectives 
Build a culture focused on customer success innovation, continuous improvement, and collaboration.
Partner with Sales, Rental and Product Support leadership to establish technology champions throughout the organization.

Performance Management:
Develop and track key performance indicators including: Technology revenue growth, VisionLink adoption, Cat Grade order rates, Subscription renewals, Customer utilization rates, Technology attachment rates, and Customer satisfaction metrics. 
Monitor profitability and ROI of technology initiatives.
Provide regular reporting to dealership leadership and Caterpillar.

Minimum Skills and Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in business, Engineering, Construction Management, Information Technology, or related field required. MBA or advanced degree preferred.
Minimum 10 years of experience in heavy equipment, construction technology, digital solutions, product support, equipment sales, or related industries.
Minimum 5 years of leadership or management experience.
Ability and willingness to travel up to 50-60% of the time, including overnight travel as needed.
Experience with Caterpillar, SITECH, Trimble, Top Con, telematics, fleet management, or construction technology preferred. 
Proven success developing and executing strategic business plans.
Demonstrated ability to lead organizational change initiatives.
Strong understanding of:
Caterpillar technology products
Telematics and connectivity solutions
Fleet management systems
Construction and mining applicants 
Product support operations

Equipment sales and rental operations
Strong financial and business acumen.
Excellent communication and presentation skills.
Ability to influence across departments and all levels of the organization.
Strong project management and change management capabilities.

Computer Consultants International, Inc. (CCI) is seeking an experienced Enterprise Project Manager Consultant to support the South Carolina Department of Public Health (SC DPH).
This role will support agency-wide project management and governance initiatives, including implementation of a new Project Management System, portfolio oversight, Power BI dashboard reporting, stakeholder engagement, user training, and organizational change management.
The ideal candidate brings extensive experience managing complex IT and business projects, supporting state or federal government initiatives, implementing project management systems, and developing dashboards that improve project visibility and decision-making.

Lead and coordinate enterprise-level IT and business projects from planning through implementation.
Support implementation and adoption of the agency's new Project Management System as the existing PWA platform is decommissioned.
Establish and maintain project management standards, governance processes, methodologies, and best practices.
Oversee project portfolios, resource coordination, project status tracking, risks, issues, and dependencies.
Create and maintain Power BI dashboards to communicate project performance, portfolio status, milestones, and management metrics.
Develop and execute change management strategies to support system implementation and organizational adoption.
Engage stakeholders across departments to gather requirements, communicate progress, and resolve project-related challenges.
Coordinate user training, documentation, and ongoing support for project management tools and processes.
Prepare project reports, executive updates, and presentations to support leadership decisions.
Support strategic initiatives aligned with the South Carolina Department of Public Health's organizational objectives.

15+ years of project management experience.

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology or Business Administration.

Experience implementing public health software or public health IT systems.
CompTIA A+ certification.

Merchant Serv is a comprehensive merchant services provider that supports businesses with payment processing, point-of-sale (POS) systems, and virtual assistance solutions. The organization focuses on reducing or eliminating processing fees so businesses can reinvest savings into growth and operations. It offers secure, affordable, and powerful POS hardware tailored to small business needs, along with tools for online transactions, invoicing, recurring billing, and acceptance of major credit cards. Merchant Serv emphasizes personalized service, with local account executives collaborating closely with business leaders nationwide to design custom plans aligned with specific objectives.
